Description: Strength of patient's conviction in target, alternative, and problematic cognitions (including automatic thoughts, core beliefs, delusions). Guides selection of interventions and measurement of change.
Intensity and type of emotional responses during session and experiments (anxiety, distress, mood swings, hopelessness, anger, etc.). Influences approach and pacing.
Presence, specificity, and frequency of behaviors aimed at reducing perceived threat (avoidance, checking, reassurance-seeking, rituals, withdrawal). Affects formulation and limits progress.
Patient's readiness, motivation, and openness to cognitive/experiential change and behavioral experiments. Determines pacing and intervention choice.
Strength of collaboration, trust, engagement, and openness between therapist and patient. Underpins all interventions and progress.
Degree of patient awareness of internal states, beliefs, emotions, and cognitive/behavioral patterns. Affects ability to recognize and challenge cognitions.

Presence and intensity of thinking distortions (catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, rumination, selective attention, misinterpretation, arbitrary inference). Guides cognitive restructuring.
Level of involvement, commitment, and follow-through with in-session and homework behavioral experiments. Indicates likelihood of therapeutic progress.
Degree of shift in conviction or emotional reaction following corrective experiences or experiments. Guides next steps and indicates learning.
Extent to which new cognitions and behaviors transfer to other contexts or situations beyond the session. Reflects long-term progress.

Variable Name: Avoidance of Affect and Emotional Disclosure
Description: Patient's ability and willingness to name, tolerate, and discuss affective states. Key for emotional processing and change.
Patient’s preparedness and willingness to participate in behavioral experiments or exposures. Determines timing and safety.
Influence of comorbid issues (depression, social anxiety, chronic pain, substance misuse, cognitive impairment) on session engagement and progress.
Extent of impairment in social, occupational, cognitive, or physical functioning due to symptoms. Guides goals and measures recovery.
Patient's current support network and degree of connection or withdrawal; involvement of significant others.

Variable Name: Risk Behaviors and Urges (Self-Injury, Substance Use, Mania)
Description: Intensity and type of urges for self-injury or risky behaviors; impact on safety planning and session focus.

Variable Name: Relapse Risk and Early Warning Signs
Description: Presence of indicators for symptom relapse or deterioration (specific to disorder and patient history). Guides prevention strategies.
Degree of bias in how patient interprets, attends to, or recalls information/data from experiments or daily life. Guides evidence evaluation.
Frequency and effectiveness of adaptive or maladaptive coping strategies (problem-solving, distraction, seeking help, self-punishment, etc.).
Agreement or discrepancy between analytical and experiential perspectives, evidence assessment, and therapy goals.
